story: It is a humid Friday evening at 6:17 in Sumter Oaks, and the air hangs hazy at 83 degrees. Gary is cheerfully fitting a speaker bracket onto his parade cart in his garage when Rosa stops by, hopeful about her Saturday dinner plans. Over on Magnolia Loop, Donna thanks Hal for clearing a notice off the community board, and the two of them settle on cornbread, cobbler, and ice cream for the weekend gathering.

gary.thought_process: Rosa just showed up while I'm out at the cart with the speaker bracket snug and the lights off. Nobody's said anything to me yet, so I should greet her instead of ignoring her. Gary's a talker and being needed is the whole point. I filed the review paperwork, so I can honestly say the cart work is squared away. Keep it short and friendly, and ask what brings her by.

parameters.content: Well, evening, Rosa! Come on in. I'm just fitting a speaker bracket on the parade cart, lights off, paperwork's already filed. What can I do for you?

donna.thought_process: Hal is right here and just asked to have his old violation notice taken down since the flamingos and cart are squared away. I tucked the extras behind the hedge, so I'm within the three-ornament limit, and I want things friendly with him before Saturday's dinner at Rosa's. I've already said my piece about the flamingos and the cobbler, so I shouldn't repeat that. A warm, short thank-you for squaring things away, plus a reminder about the ice cream, keeps the peace and moves things forward.

parameters.content: Thanks for clearing that notice off the board, Hal, I appreciate it. Now go enjoy your evening, and I'll see you Saturday with the ice cream!

hal.thought_process: Donna's right there and says the extra flamingos are tucked behind the hedge. I already took down my old notice, so the matter's closed. Rosa and I settled on Saturday, and the cornbread and my good chair are ready. Nothing left to harp on. A short civil word to Donna about tomorrow keeps things friendly and doesn't repeat what anyone's already said. She did me the courtesy of fixing it, so I'll acknowledge it.

parameters.content: Noted, Donna. Three showing from the street is what the code says, and I appreciate you seeing to it. I'll bring the cornbread tomorrow, and you save me a scoop of that ice cream.

rosa.thought_process: I'm at Gary's house and he's right here. Hal and Donna are both confirmed for Saturday, Hal's coming at four tomorrow to carry the table, and Donna has the dessert covered. Gary is the last one I haven't pinned down, and he's the stalling one. I shouldn't ask him a vague 'are you coming' again. Better to give him an easy, concrete job so he feels part of it, and lock in a time.

parameters.content: Gary, Hal's bringing cornbread and Donna's got the cobbler, so you're my last seat at the table. Saturday at five, and if you bring a bag of ice and your folding chairs, you're all set.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
